desc: Derive the row-prefix monotone formulation and interval-scan feasibility criterion.

Implement the complete Python solution: parse stdin, aggregate per-row `L`/`U` bounds, reject `L>U`, sort constrained rows and scan with running `minU`, print `Yes`/`No`, with concise proof comments and `O(M log M)` time / `O(M)` memory.
Validate against tiny brute-force enumeration and targeted edge cases: `N=1`, `W` at `y=1`, `B` at `y=N`, mixed clues in one row, reverse-order row conflict, and large sparse `N`.
Final review for off-by-one errors, exact stdout casing, and no grid materialization for `N` up to `1e9`.
